discussion.body:
## Rough Summary

A `GeoSet` contains a group of physics objects (`Primitives`)
The "grouping" is done with the common `.first_X`, `.num_X` system
Each `Primitive` appears only once, but `GeoSets` appear multiple times
> NOTE: `GeoSets` can also embed a single `Primitive` within themselves

`Grid` & `GridCells` index `GeoSets` a few spans at a time
This means some `GeoSets` are duplicates
Each duplicate has the same `straddle_group` value
Seems to be an ID to aid with caching `GeoSets`
I haven't done any reverse engineering of engine `.dll`s to confirm this

`Grid.num_straddle_groups` matches the maximum `straddle_group` value + 1
A value of `0` is commonly used for `GeoSets` with no duplicates (unique to their parent `GridCell`)
> NOTE: A map with a `Grid.num_straddle_groups` value that is too low will run in Northstar
> -- spawned players are frozen in place without crashing


### Lump Relationships

```
Grid -> GridCell -> GeoSet -> Primitive
                                                          
         /-> UniqueContents
Primitive -> .type -> Brush OR Tricoll OR StaticProp
                                                          
GeoSets can contain duplicates (use same .straddle_group)
GeoSets is parallel w/ GeoSetBounds
Primitives is parallel w/ PrimitiveBounds
PrimitiveBounds & GeoSetBounds use the same "Bounds" type
```
> NOTE: `TricollNodes` also uses the same "Bounds" type (Oriented)
> -- Brushes also use a `.origin` + `.extents` model to define their bounds (Axis-Aligned)

Presumably each straddle group covers a unique combination of GridCells

It's worth noting that some maps use the `Models[0]` GridCell
This doesn't make much sense to me, as the base grid should cover all worldspawn geo

it gets copied for each `GridCell` that needs to index other `GeoSet`s

in every single map, there is only 1 `Primitive` per static prop
so `GeoSet`s need to grab a sequence of props that appear in roughly the same area

`straddle_group` `243` shares `GridCell` `767` w/ `straddle_group` `242`
`bsp_regen` should try to use a similar system for grouping props

looking at r2 `mp_glitch` `GridCell` 6 (`GeoSet` 3244 / Straddle Group 432)
![glitch_tricoll_568](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b4370edb-2e30-443d-9a6e-9e2a97f9f366)

`GeoSetBounds` wraps the `TriColl` (568), while `PrimitiveBounds` (5999) is at a 45 degree angle
The triangular pocket this outlines is really tight, any ray test is highly unlikely to fail

`bsp_regen` is far lazier in it's approach, using an AABB for each level & wrapping the `GeoSetBounds` around it's child `PrimitiveBounds`

Idk what kind of algorithm respawn developed to get this combination of YOBBs to create such a tight hull, but it's very cool
When I first visualised the bounds I was confused by the `PrimitiveBounds` not being fully contained in `GeoSetBounds`

Also worth noting that `Tricoll` has it's own tree of `TricollNodes` to minimise the number of tests for a ray miss

"Graze" seems like a good word for near-hits
when the game engine gets partway through testing a BVH tree before recognising the miss

## Straddle Groups
 - `0` unused?
 - `1` `Brushes[0 & 3]` (+/- Z)
   * `GridCells[0..3]`
 - `2` `Brushes[1]` (+Y)
   * `GridCells[2 & 3]`
 - `3` `Brushes[2]` (+X)
   * `GridCells[1 & 3]`
 - `4` `Brushes[4]` (-Y)
   * `GridCell[0 & 1]`
 - `5` `Brushes[5]` (-X)
   * `GridCell[0 & 2]`
